fields.corePath: The coach of a cricket academy opens the site on his phone at the ground. Step 1, he taps Try a demo batch, or if it is his own academy he taps New batch and types the batch name and the players, one name per line. Step 2, the batch page opens showing today's date at the top and every player as a big row. Step 3, he taps a player's row once for Present, twice for Absent, three times for Late — the row changes colour each time and the count at the top updates. Step 4, he taps Save today's attendance. Step 5, the page flips to This month, where every player has a strip of thirty small boxes, green for present and grey for absent, and a percentage on the right. Step 6, he taps Send to parents, which gives him one WhatsApp message per absent player, already written, with the player's name and how many sessions they have missed this month. Step 7, he taps Download month as CSV if he wants it for the academy's records. The demo batch does all of this with fourteen made-up players so nobody needs to create anything to see it work.
fields.knownGaps: Attendance is by date and one session a day. Two of the academies I showed it to run a morning and an evening batch for the same player, and right now that has to be two separate batches with the same names typed twice. That is the biggest real gap. There is no edit-yesterday screen — if he marks someone present by mistake and saves, he can fix it by opening that date from the month view, but it takes four taps and nobody finds it without being told. The month view only renders the current month, last month is in the CSV but not on screen. Player names have no photos, so two boys named Arjun in one batch are genuinely confusing and one coach has been writing "Arjun (tall)". The WhatsApp messages are copy-one-at-a-time, not a bulk send. Data lives in Postgres against the batch code with no login, same trade-off as the order-book idea — the code is the password. CSV download does not work in the in-app browser you get when you open a link from WhatsApp itself, which is exactly where half my coaches open it; they have to open in Chrome first. None of this blocks marking and saving a day, which is the thing they actually do every evening.
